subject: general
question: The festival of Navratri is associated with the worship of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goddess Durga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The festival of **Navratri** is one of the most significant **Hindu** festivals, primarily dedicated to the worship of **Goddess Durga**. The word **Navratri** is derived from **Sanskrit**, where **'Nava'** means **nine** and **'Ratri'** means **nights**.
 
• The festival spans over **nine nights** and **ten days**, during which **nine** distinct forms of the **Goddess**, known as **Navadurga**, are invoked and worshipped.
 
• It celebrates the victory of **Goddess Durga** over the buffalo demon **Mahishasura**. This battle signifies the triumph of **Dharma** (righteousness) over **Adharma** (evil). ***Hence, the correct answer is Goddess Durga.***
 
• While there are **four** seasonal **Navratris** in a **year**, the most prominent one is **Sharada Navratri**, which typically falls in the **lunar month** of **Ashvin** (corresponding to **September** or **October** in the **Gregorian calendar**).
 
• Each of the **nine** days is associated with a specific **color** and a specific incarnation of the **Goddess**, including **Shailaputri**, **Brahmacharini**, **Chandraghanta**, **Kushmanda**, **Skandamata**, **Katyayani**, **Kaalratri**, **Mahagauri**, and **Siddhidhatri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional Celebrations:**
 
 
• In **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Assam**, the festival is celebrated as **Durga Puja**, where grand **pandals** are created to house clay idols of the **Goddess**.
 
• In **Gujarat**, the festival is marked by traditional dances known as **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, where people dance in circles around a lamp or an image of the **Goddess**.
 
• In **North India**, the **Ramleela** (dramatic enactment of the **Ramayana**) is performed, culminating in **Dussehra**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Tenth Day:**
 
 
• The **tenth** day is celebrated as **Vijayadashami** or **Dussehra**. It marks the day **Goddess Durga** killed **Mahishasura** and also the day **Lord Rama** defeated the demon king **Ravana**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Navratri:**
 
 
• **Chaitra Navratri:** Celebrated in the **month** of **Chaitra** (**March**-**April**), it marks the beginning of the **Hindu New Year** (**Vikram Samvat**).
 
• **Magha** and **Ashada Navratri:** These are known as **Gupta Navratri**, which are observed primarily by **Sadhakas** and **Tantriks** for spiritual practices.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism:**
 
 
• **Goddess Durga** is often depicted with **eight** or **ten** arms, riding a **lion** or **tiger**, and carrying various weapons, representing her **Shakti** (feminine power) and protective nature.
